title: fix(cors)!: one CORS admission rule at every door — createHonoApp's default, loopback beside a list, all-host patterns, auth's trusted origins
body:
Fixes #24809
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

## What changes

Every door in this repository that mounts CORS or reads `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` now gives one configuration one answer. The governing text is `docs/HARDENING.md` § CORS: "Do **not** use `origin: '*'` with `credentials: true`", and the go-live checklist's "CORS origin list is explicit, not `*`". #24738's Expected adds: "Localhost stays admitted in dev only, if at all." This PR closes the family #24738 (PR #24806) opened, at the four locations the card and its comment `6288561947` name.

- **One rule.** `resolveCorsAdmission` (new, `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/cors-admission.ts`) decides what a transport door admits from the door's own options and the `OS_CORS_*` environment. `HonoServerPlugin` reads it in `init()`. `@objectstack/hono`'s `createHonoApp` reads it when the app is created. Each door only maps its own option names (`cors.origins` and `cors.origin`) onto it, and nothing is copied.
- **Location 1, `createHonoApp`.** Its old default was the combination #24738 removed from `HonoServerPlugin`: with no list, every origin was admitted with credentials, and `'*'` with credentials on was accepted. It now answers exactly as `HonoServerPlugin` does.
- **Location 2, loopback beside a list.** `matchOriginPattern` admitted every loopback origin ahead of any pattern, in every mode. It now matches the pattern and nothing else. `createOriginMatcher` admits a loopback origin beside a non-empty list on a development boot only.
- **Location 3, all-host patterns.** `isAllHostOriginPattern` (new) names `'*'` and a pattern whose host part is the bare `*`: `https://*`, `*://*`, `http://*:*`, `https://*:8443`. With credentials on, any such entry is refused exactly as `'*'` is, and the message names the entry.
- **Location 4, auth's trusted origins.** `auth-manager.ts` tested the whole `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` value against `'*'` and split it afterwards. It now judges each entry, and an entry that admits every host never enters better-auth's trusted origins. Only that block is touched. `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`, the preview and root-domain wildcards, SSO discovery and the development substitution are unchanged.
- **The enumeration pin.** `packages/qa/http-conformance/src/cors-doors.conformance.test.ts` lists the three doors and asks each one the same nine configurations.

The development boot is `isDevelopmentBoot` from `@objectstack/core` (`NODE_ENV` exactly `development`), the reading PR #24806 uses. The rule reads it once and passes it to the matcher. The matcher takes it as an optional `{ developmentBoot }`. When that option is omitted, the matcher reads the same signal when it is created. That default is deliberate. The cloud's serverless preflight short-circuit imports `createOriginMatcher` with one argument, so it now follows the matcher's new answer and agrees with the transport on the same boot without a change there. An option that defaulted to `false` would have made that preflight refuse loopback on a development boot while the transport admitted it, which is the preflight-versus-request divergence the module header records. The cross-repo consumer is NOT MEASURED from here.

## Contract

Every input whose answer changes. "Admitted" means the origin is echoed in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. "Development boot" means `NODE_ENV` is exactly `development`.

| Door | Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `createHonoApp` | No list, credentials on (the default), not a development boot | every origin admitted, with credentials | no cross-origin caller admitted |
| `createHonoApp` | No list, credentials on, development boot | every origin admitted, with credentials | loopback origins only, with credentials |
| `createHonoApp` | No list, `OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS=false`, not a development boot | every origin admitted, without credentials | no cross-origin caller admitted |
| `createHonoApp` | No list, `OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS=false`, development boot | every origin admitted, without credentials | loopback origins only, without credentials |
| `createHonoApp` | A list holding `*` (option or `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`, alone or among other entries), credentials on | created; every origin admitted, with credentials | `createHonoApp` throws |
| `HonoServerPlugin`, `createHonoApp` | A list holding a pattern whose host part is the bare `*`, credentials on | booted; every host the pattern matches admitted, with credentials | `init()` throws and the boot fails, or `createHonoApp` throws |
| `HonoServerPlugin`, `createHonoApp` | A list with at least one pattern, not a development boot | the list, plus every loopback origin | the list only |
| `HonoServerPlugin` | A list of exact origins only, not a development boot | the list, plus every loopback origin | the list only |
| `createHonoApp` | A list of exact origins only, development boot | the list only | the list, plus loopback origins (a gain, development boot only) |
| `createHonoApp` | The `cors.origin` option as one comma-separated string of exact origins (no `*`), credentials on or off | no origin admitted (`OS_CORS_ORIGIN` written the same way was already split, and is unchanged) | each listed origin admitted, and on a development boot loopback origins too, as in the row above (a widening under the `yes` line, only toward what the operator listed, which the option's TSDoc already promised: "Comma-separated string or array"; the one exception to the exact-origin line under "Unchanged") |
| `AuthManager` (plugin-auth) | `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` holding `*` among other entries | `*` entered better-auth's trusted origins | `*` is dropped; the other entries are trusted as before |
| `AuthManager` | `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` of `*` written with surrounding space | `*` entered the trusted origins | nothing enters from it |
| `AuthManager` | `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` holding a pattern whose host part is the bare `*` | the pattern entered the trusted origins | the pattern is dropped |

Unchanged:

- An exact origin, or a pattern that names part of the host (`https://*.example.com`, `http://localhost:*`), is admitted as before, with or without credentials, at both transport doors, and auth trusts it as before.
- On a development boot, `HonoServerPlugin` admits loopback origins beside a list as before. With no list, `HonoServerPlugin` answers as #24738 left it.
- `*`, or an all-host pattern, with credentials off still boots and admits without credentials.
- An empty list (`cors.origins: []`, or `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` of whitespace) admits nothing, loopback included, in every mode, as before.
- `cors: false`, `cors.enabled: false` and `OS_CORS_ENABLED=false` still mount nothing. Allowed and exposed headers, methods and max-age are unchanged. Preflights are still answered `204`, admitted or not.
- Same-origin requests are outside CORS, so the Console and every page the server serves are unaffected. `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` admits nothing to CORS (ruling A, `6288093770`).

**Public surface added (outside the table).** `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` gains these exports so that one rule is shared by two published doors, `HonoServerPlugin` and `createHonoApp`. They, and the `createHonoApp` development-boot row above, are why the `Clause-②` line reads `yes`:

- `resolveCorsAdmission`, with its types `CorsAdmission`, `CorsAdmissionInput` and `CorsAdmissionDoor`;
- `isAllHostOriginPattern`;
- `OriginMatcherOptions`, the type of `createOriginMatcher`'s new optional second parameter.

The refusal message now names the entry, and `createHonoApp` gains the refusal. Nothing is removed or renamed, and no spec key moves.

## Mechanism (measured)

- **Before-state, per location.** The new pins were committed first, as `a9c5f629a` (base `b3fc122f0` plus the test files only), and run against that tree's source. `plugin-hono-server` and `@objectstack/hono` were run from source, and `http-conformance` from a `dist/` built at that commit:
  - `plugin-hono-server` `src/cors-default-admission.test.ts`: `Tests 5 failed | 15 passed (20)`. In each failure, a loopback origin beside a list was admitted outside development, or an all-host pattern with credentials booted.
  - `@objectstack/hono` `src/hono-cors-admission.test.ts`: `Tests 7 failed | 3 passed (10)`. A foreign origin was echoed with no list, a loopback origin beside an exact list was not admitted on a development boot, and `createHonoApp` did not throw for `*` or an all-host pattern with credentials.
  - `plugin-auth` `src/auth-manager.cors-origin-trust.test.ts`: `Tests 3 failed | 1 passed (4)`. In each failure, the trusted origins held `*` or an all-host pattern.
  - `http-conformance` `src/cors-doors.conformance.test.ts`: `Tests 11 failed | 7 passed (18)`.
  - After the fix, all four files passed (see Tests).
- **What better-auth does with an all-host entry.** The card's mechanism note said this was not verified. It was measured on the installed better-auth `1.7.3`, using `matchesOriginPattern` in `dist/auth/trusted-origins.mjs`. better-auth reads `https://*` and `*://*` each as matching every origin of their scheme, as it reads `*` (and `https://*.*` nearly so). So an all-host pattern in the trusted set has the same effect as `*`, and auth drops the same narrow class the transport refuses. Auth does not depend on `plugin-hono-server`, so its block carries a one-line predicate of the same class. The enumeration pin holds the two equal. No other non-origin entry is judged.
- **"Host part is the bare `*`", defined narrowly.** It is the regular expression in `isAllHostOriginPattern`: an optional `scheme://`, then only `*` characters, then an optional `:port` or `:*`. A pattern that names any part of the host is not in the class, including `https://*.*`. No general pattern validator is added.
- **Location 2's consumers in this repo.** Two places relied on loopback beside a list outside development, and both were the matcher's own unit tests in `pattern-matcher.test.ts` ("should always allow localhost origins regardless of configured patterns", and `127.0.0.1` beside `http://localhost:*`). They pinned the old convenience, and they now pin the development-only rule. No other test, example or shipped code relies on it:
  - the only `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` assertions in the repo are `@objectstack/hono`'s `hono.test.ts`, whose loopback case names `http://localhost:*` in its own list, and `plugin-hono-server`'s pin file;
  - no example configures a CORS list;
  - objectui's console reaches the API same-origin (its Vite `/api` proxy in dev, and `VITE_SERVER_URL` empty in both `.env` files; read-only, `../objectui` at `cd4623d06`).
- **The doors.** A grep of `packages/` for non-test readers of `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` and importers of `hono/cors` returns three doors: `hono-plugin.ts`, `adapters/hono/src/index.ts` and `auth-manager.ts`. No other adapter mounts CORS.

## Tests

All runs are on `fb509fc0a` (this branch merged with `origin/main` `9a06f0be0`) unless a line names another commit. `bb2fde296`, the head this PR opens with, differs from it only in the changeset's text. The pins, by what they assert:

- `plugin-hono-server` `src/cors-default-admission.test.ts`, describes 5 and 6:
  - outside development, a list admits what it names and no loopback origin, whether the list comes from the option or from `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`;
  - on a development boot, a loopback origin is admitted beside the list;
  - a list that names `http://localhost:*` admits it in every mode, and nothing else;
  - each all-host pattern, alone or in a list, by option or by env, is refused in `init()`, and the message names the entry and both remedies;
  - an all-host pattern without credentials boots;
  - `https://*.example.com` boots with credentials.
- `plugin-hono-server` `src/pattern-matcher.test.ts`:
  - `matchOriginPattern` matches the pattern only;
  - `createOriginMatcher` admits loopback beside a list on a development boot only, and an empty list admits nothing;
  - the default development reading is `NODE_ENV` exactly `development`, read at creation;
  - `isAllHostOriginPattern` names the class and not its neighbours.
- `@objectstack/hono` `src/hono-cors-admission.test.ts`: `createHonoApp` answers rows 1 to 3 of the plugin's pin file the same way, with its refusal thrown when the app is created.
- `plugin-auth` `src/auth-manager.cors-origin-trust.test.ts`, read off a real better-auth instance:
  - a `*` entry among real origins, a spaced `*`, and each all-host pattern never enter the trusted origins;
  - the real origins and a host-naming pattern do.
- `http-conformance` `src/cors-doors.conformance.test.ts`, for each of nine configurations:
  - both transport doors give the same answer (refused, or the same admitted probe origins and credentials flag), and it is the row's answer;
  - auth trusts exactly the row's listed entries, and never `*` or `https://*`.

Suite runs, each command exiting 0:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server test`: 35 files, 448 tests passed. `typecheck` passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/hono test`: 12 files, 225 tests passed. `typecheck` passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 171 files, 3264 passed and 10 skipped. `typecheck` passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/http-conformance exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 19 files, 246 tests passed. `typecheck` passed.
- Each new test file is listed by its package's `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles`.

## Changeset

`.changeset/24809-cors-doors-one-admission-rule.md` bumps `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/hono` and `@objectstack/plugin-auth` as `minor` (the `fixed` group; on `main` it is at `18.0.0`, versioned in `06cab4849` and tagged, and `.changeset/pre.json` is gone, so no pre-release tag applies). It is marked **BREAKING**: an accept-set narrowing shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention. It carries the `Clause-②` line and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, the same form #24738's changeset uses. Its before and after bullets match the Contract table, and it names the development-boot gain at `createHonoApp`. `@objectstack/http-conformance` is private and gains only a test, a devDependency on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and a source alias for it. `18.0.0` was versioned after this branch's merge base, so the next version pass consumes this changeset, not `18.0.0`; landing waits on the maintainer's word.

## Acceptance notes

- **Release.** `18.0.0` is versioned (`06cab4849`, `chore: version packages`) and tagged, after this branch's merge base, so this changeset is consumed by the next version pass. Landing waits on the maintainer's word (the seat's ACCEPT `6291362699`, item 2), which also covers whether `18.0.0` closed the launch window the `minor` grade rests on; until then `minor` with the **BREAKING** banner is the form the gate enforces on `main`. Built as if it lands on `main` now.
- **The roster is declared, not discovered.** The enumeration pin lists the three doors measured at the base. A new door is caught only when it is added to `DOORS`. Discovering doors by scanning every package's source would need a cross-package input radius over all of `packages/**/src` (`check:cross-package-test-inputs`), and that would put this suite on every PR. That is a new gate, so it is not added here.
- **`content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`** (`OS_CORS_ORIGIN` row) says "`*` is refused at boot unless `OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS=false`". That is still true, but it does not name the all-host patterns. It is outside this claim's docs face. The `cli.mdx` "(CORS)" line is held off as before.
- **A stale comment inside the auth block.** "When CORS allows all origins (default)" above the development substitution predates #24738. That behaviour is held off, so the comment is left as it is.
- **The wildcard note in `serve.ts`** (about `:4182`) says better-auth's glob does not cross dot separators. Measured on `1.7.3`, it does: `https://*.example.com` matches `https://a.b.example.com`. This is pre-existing, outside this diff, and a docs precision at most.
- **`https://*.*`** matches nearly every public host at both matchers. It is outside the narrow class by design, and is reported here, not refused.
- **Cloud.** The preflight short-circuit follows `createOriginMatcher`'s new answer. A cloud deployment that relied on loopback beside its list outside development names those origins. NOT MEASURED from here.
